text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert PD#82317 fired: repeated CUDA OOMs detected on node eu-gpu-3 (kvcache surge). Error rate spike at 04:09 UTC. Auto-retry failing, requests dropping.

pagerduty-bot: PD#82317 assigned to ashley-w (on-call). Escalation in 15m if not acknowledged.

ashley-w: ack — looking now. any customer-facing errors reported? :eyes:

samir: seeing 502s in front-proxy churn for a handful of routes (chat/generate). spike in gpu_mem_alloc_failed in logs. attaching quick tail:
```
2026-11-03T04:08:31Z ERROR cuda: alloc failed: out of memory (requested 4200MB) pod=riff-abc123 container=runtime
2026-11-03T04:08:31Z WARN kvcache: evict miss growth rate 3.8x window=60s
```

priya-m: metric panels: gpu memory free pct dropped from ~24% -> 3% over 2m. Autoscaler didn't catch because node daemonset pinned GPU resources.

ashley-w: ok. immediate plan: 1) cordon eu-gpu-3 2) drain non-prod pods 3) fallback matching requests to smaller-quantized variant or cpu fallback for retries 4) notify customers if >30% user impact.

dylan-s: I can cordon/drain. Running: `kubectl cordon eu-gpu-3 && kubectl drain eu-gpu-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30`

samir: quick config check — we have a kvcache size bump in this node group (recent experiment). That plus high-concurrency batching probably caused the KV cache to balloon and exhaust allocations.

priya-m: starting canary fallback policy now: reroute model variant redwood-llama-13b-q5 -> redwood-llama-13b-q4-lite for new requests in eu region. This will reduce mem use but increase latency slightly.

incident-bot: action logged: route override applied by priya-m for service=chat/generate region=eu.

pagerduty-bot: PD#82317 acknowledged by ashley-w at 04:11 UTC.

ashley-w: draining node in progress. if drain hangs, we'll evict pods force after 60s. keep an eye on queue/backpressure to avoid thundering.

samir: observed immediate drop in cuda OOM errors after route override and start of drain. error rate down 70% in 90s.

dylan-s: drain completed. restarted a stray operator pod that held a pinned allocation. Reclaimed ~9GB GPU mem.

priya-m: starting post-mortem note: suspected root cause = kvcache growth + batching spike + recent kvcache size experiment. Will roll back config on eu-gpu pool and add autoscaling breakpoint.

ashley-w: notif to customers: drafting status update on status.redwood.ai -> "We are experiencing degraded performance for some inference requests in eu-west. Mitigation in progress; fallbacks applied. No data loss."

samir: customer impact: roughly 18% of generate requests in eu experienced retries or 502s for a 6-minute window. no global spillover.

dylan-s: adding temporary guardrail: throttle max-concurrency for q5 models to 32 on that pool. command: `redwoodctl set-rate-limit --pool eu-gpu-3 --model q5 --concurrency 32`

incident-bot: note added: handoff scheduled in 25m to next oncall (dylan-s).

ashley-w: good. I'll keep PD open until we validate root fix. priya, samir, dylan — please add logs/snippets to the incident doc (inc/PD-82317) and assign follow-ups for config rollback and kvcache limits.

priya-m: created follow-up tasks: rollback kvcache-experiment + add kvcache eviction soft-limit + alert on sustained kvcache growth.

samir: pushed a short-term Grafana alert: when gpu_free_pct < 8% for 30s AND kvcache_growth_rate > 2 -> page oncall. reduces noisy pages.

pagerduty-bot: PD#82317 status: acknowledged -> investigating.

dylan-s: final check: traffic back to normal, latencies slightly higher for q4-lite. no further OOMs in last 5m.

ashley-w: marking this thread for follow-up. leaving PD open until postmortem draft ready. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
